text: If m and n respectively are the number of local maximum and local minimum points of the function $f(x)=\int\limits _{0}^{x^{2}}\frac{t^{2}-5t+4}{2+e^{t}}dt$, then the ordered pair (m, n) is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x)=\int\limits _{0}^{x^{2}}\frac{t^{2}-5t+4}{2+e^{t}}dt$

$f^{'}(x)=2x\left (\frac{x^{4}-5x^{2}+4}{2+e^{x2}}\right )=0$

$x=0$, or $(x^{2}-4)(x^{2}-1)=0$

$x=0,$ $x=\pm 2,\pm 1$

Now, $f^{'}(x)=\frac{2x(x+1)(x-1)(x+2)(x-2)}{\left (e^{x2}+2\right )}$

f'(x) changes sign from positive to negative at x = $-$1, 1 So, number of local maximum points = 2

f'(x) changes sign from negative to positive at x = $-$2, 0, 2 So, number of local minimum points = 3

$\therefore$ m = 2, n = 3

text: The integral $\int\limits _{0}^{1}\frac{1}{7^{\left [\dfrac{1}{x}\right ]}}dx$, where [ . ] denotes the greatest integer function, is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\int\limits _{0}^{1}\frac{1}{7^{\left [\dfrac{1}{x}\right ]}}dx$, let $\frac{1}{x}=t$

$\frac{-1}{x^{2}}dx=dt$

$=\int\limits _{\infty }^{1}\frac{1}{-t^{2}7^{[t]}}dt=\int\limits _{1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{t^{2}7^{[t]}}dt$

$=\int\limits _{1}^{2}\frac{1}{7t^{2}}dt+\int\limits _{2}^{3}\frac{1}{7^{2}t^{2}}dt+....$

$=\frac{1}{7}\left [-\frac{1}{t}\right ]_{1}^{2}+\frac{1}{7^{2}}\left [\frac{-1}{t}\right ]_{2}^{3}+\frac{1}{7^{3}}\left [-\frac{1}{t}\right ]_{2}^{3}+....$

$=\sum\limits _{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{7^{n}}\left (\frac{1}{n}-\frac{1}{n+1}\right )$

$=\sum\limits _{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{\left (\frac{1}{7}\right )^{n}}{n}-7\sum\limits _{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{\left (\frac{1}{7}\right )^{n+1}}{n+1}$

$=-\log \left (1-\frac{1}{7}\right )+7\log \left (1-\frac{1}{7}\right )+1$

$=1+6\log \frac{6}{7}$

and given parabola

$\therefore$ a = 9, b = $-$6, c = 134, d = $-$2, k = $-$711

text: $α=\sin 36^{\circ }$ is a root of which of the following equation?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given that $α=\sin 36^{\circ }$, we need to determine which equation it is a root of.

We start with the known relationship for $\cos 72^{\circ }$:

$\cos 72^{\circ }=\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{4}$

Using the double-angle formula for cosine:

$\cos 72^{\circ }=1-2\sin ^{2}36^{\circ }$

Substitute $α$ for $\sin 36^{\circ }$:

$1-2α^{2}=\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{4}$

Multiply both sides by 4:

$4-8α^{2}=\sqrt{5}-1$

Add 1 to both sides:

$5-8α^{2}=\sqrt{5}$

Square both sides to eliminate the radical:

$(5-8α^{2})^{2}=5$

Expand the left side:

$25+64α^{4}-80α^{2}=5$

Simplify by subtracting 5 from both sides:

$64α^{4}-80α^{2}+20=0$

Divide the entire equation by 4:

$16α^{4}-20α^{2}+5=0$

Thus, the equation $16α^{4}-20α^{2}+5=0$ is the one for which $α=\sin 36^{\circ }$ is a root.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift

text: Let $α$, $β$ be the roots of the equation $x^{2}-4λx+5=0$ and $α$, $γ$ be the roots of the equation $x^{2}-\left (3\sqrt{2}+2\sqrt{3}\right )x+7+3λ\sqrt{3}=0$, $λ$ > 0. If $β+γ=3\sqrt{2}$, then $(α+2β+γ)^{2}$ is equal to $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
From the two equations, $α+β=4λ$, $αβ=5$ and $α+γ=3\sqrt{2}+2\sqrt{3}$.

Adding the two sums, $2α+(β+γ)=4λ+3\sqrt{2}+2\sqrt{3}$; with $β+γ=3\sqrt{2}$ this gives $α=2λ+\sqrt{3}$.

Since $α$ is a root of $x^{2}-4λx+5=0$:

$(2λ+\sqrt{3})^{2}-4λ(2λ+\sqrt{3})+5=0\Rightarrow -4λ^{2}+8=0\Rightarrow λ=\sqrt{2}(λ>0)$

Then $α=2\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{3}$, which also satisfies the second equation: $α^{2}-(3\sqrt{2}+2\sqrt{3})α+7+3\sqrt{6}=(11+4\sqrt{6})-(18+7\sqrt{6})+7+3\sqrt{6}=0$.

$α+2β+γ=(α+β)+(β+γ)=4\sqrt{2}+3\sqrt{2}=7\sqrt{2}$

$(α+2β+γ)^{2}=(7\sqrt{2})^{2}=98$

Hence, the answer is 98.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift

text: Let A be a matrix of order 2 $\times$ 2, whose entries are from the set {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5}. If the sum of all the entries of A is a prime number p, 2 < p < 8, then the number of such matrices A is $___________$.

solution.body:

If sum is 3 then possible entries are (0, 0, 0, 3), (0, 0, 1, 2) or (0, 1, 1, 1).

$\therefore$ Total number of matrices = 4  + 4 + 12 = 20

If sum of 5 then possible entries are

$\therefore$ Total number of matrices = 4 + 12 + 12 + 12 + 12 + 4 = 56

If sum is 7 then possible entries are

(0, 0, 2, 5), (0, 0, 3, 4), (0, 1, 1, 5), (0, 3, 3, 1), (0, 2, 2, 3), (1, 1, 1, 4), (1, 2, 2, 2), (1, 1, 2, 3) and (0, 1, 2, 4).

Total number of matrices with sum 7 = 104

$\therefore$ Total number of required matrices

= 20 + 56 + 104

= 180

solution.body:
$y=(x^{x})^{x}=x^{x^{2}}$, so $\ln y=x^{2}\ln x$.

Differentiating: $\dfrac{1}{y}\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2x\ln x+x$, so

$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=x^{x^{2}+1}(1+2\ln x)$

At $x=1$: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=1$.

Write $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=uv$ with $u=x^{x^{2}+1}$ and $v=1+2\ln x$. From $\ln u=(x^{2}+1)\ln x$, $u^{'}=u\left (2x\ln x+\dfrac{x^{2}+1}{x}\right )$, and $v^{'}=\dfrac{2}{x}$. At $x=1$: $u=1$, $u^{'}=2$, $v=1$, $v^{'}=2$.

$\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\left |_{x=1}=u^{'}v+uv^{'}=2+2=4 \right.$

Since $\dfrac{dx}{dy}=\left (\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right )^{-1}$,

$\dfrac{d^{2}x}{dy^{2}}=\dfrac{d}{dx}\left [\left (\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right )^{-1}\right ]\dfrac{dx}{dy}=-\dfrac{d^{2}y/dx^{2}}{(dy/dx)^{3}}$

At $x=1$: $\dfrac{d^{2}x}{dy^{2}}=-\dfrac{4}{1^{3}}=-4$, so $\dfrac{d^{2}x}{dy^{2}}+20=16$.

Hence, the answer is 16.

text: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $(1-x^{2})dy=\left (xy+(x^{3}+2)\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\right )dx,-1<x<1$, and $y(0)=0$. If $\int\limits _{\frac{-1}{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}}\sqrt{1-x^{2}}y(x)dx=k$, then $k^{-1}$ is equal to $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\left (1-x^{2}\right )dy=\left (xy+\left (x^{3}+2\right )\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\right )dx$

$\therefore$ $\frac{dy}{dx}-\frac{x}{1-x^{2}}y=\frac{x^{3}+2}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}$

$\therefore$ $I.F.=e^{\int -\frac{x}{1-x2}dx}=\sqrt{1-x^{2}}$

Solution is

$y.\sqrt{1-x^{2}}=\int \left (x^{3}+2\right )dx$

$y.\sqrt{1-x^{2}}=\frac{x^{4}}{4}+2x+c$

$\because$ $y(0)=0\Rightarrow c=0$

$\therefore$ $y(x)=\frac{x^{4}+8x}{4\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}$

text: Let $S = {E_{1}, E_{2}, ........., E_{8}}$ be a sample space of a random experiment such that $P(E_{n})=\frac{n}{36}$ for every n = 1, 2, ........, 8. Then the number of elements in the set $\left \{A\subseteq S:P(A)\geq \frac{4}{5}\right \}$ is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$P(E_{1})+P(E_{2})+\cdots +P(E_{8})=\dfrac{1+2+\cdots +8}{36}=1$, and for $A\subseteq S$, $P(A)=\dfrac{s}{36}$, where $s$ is the sum of the indices $n$ of the outcomes $E_{n}$ in $A$.

$P(A)\geq \frac{4}{5}\Rightarrow s\geq \frac{144}{5}=28.8\Rightarrow s\geq 29$

The complement $S\setminus A$ then has index sum $36-s\leq 7$, and each such complement gives exactly one $A$.

Subsets of $\{1,2,\ldots ,8\}$ with sum at most 7, listed by sum:

$\begin{array}{ll} 0 & :\emptyset (1) \\ 1 & :\{1\}(1) \\ 2 & :\{2\}(1) \\ 3 & :\{3\},\{1,2\}(2) \\ 4 & :\{4\},\{1,3\}(2) \\ 5 & :\{5\},\{1,4\},\{2,3\}(3) \\ 6 & :\{6\},\{1,5\},\{2,4\},\{1,2,3\}(4) \\ 7 & :\{7\},\{1,6\},\{2,5\},\{3,4\},\{1,2,4\}(5) \end{array}$

$\text{Number of sets}A=1+1+1+2+2+3+4+5=19$

Hence, the answer is 19.
